items.sentence: On [MASK], Complainant filed an EEO complaint alleging that the Agency discriminated against her based on race (African-American) when she was terminated from her probationary position on August 2, 2018.

At the hearing, Complainant testified that her second-level supervisor (S2), Department Head, GS- 0301-12, “made the decision to terminate her after learning that her ‘significant other’ was [W]hite.” Complainant testified that S2 became aware of Complainant’s relationship with a White man in [MASK], and that her relationship with S2 changed afterward.

She also testified that her first-level supervisor (S1), Professional Affairs Coordinator (Assistant Department Head), GS-0301-11, “had warned [Complainant] not to let [S2] know she was dating a [W]hite man.” To corroborate her theory that S2 discriminated against her based on her race, Complainant presented a key witness, a coworker (CW), Program Analyst, GS-0303-07, who “testified that [[MASK]] openly stated that [S2’s] husband was extremely biased against interracial relationships, and that she was surprised Complainant was dating a [W]hite man. [CW] claims she heard [S2] make other race-related remarks.” Both Complainant and CW testified that S1 had warned them about S2’s prejudice. 2 The AJ found this testimony lacked credibility “due to the glaring omission of any theory about Complainant’s interracial relationship in her complaint, EEO counseling records, or her affidavit [during the investigation].” The AJ reasoned that “[t]his type of evidence, if credible, would not have come up for the first time some three years after her termination.” During EEO counseling and in her affidavit, Complainant explained that she believed her termination stemmed from events that occurred during a work conference in Leesburg, Virginia, where S2 allegedly engaged in inappropriate behavior, and Complainant believed that S2 “did not trust [her] to not share what happened.” Complainant also had indicated that her termination was related to the fact that S2 thought Complainant had filed a grievance against her, though it had been another employee.
[MASK] testified during the hearing and denied making any comments about S2 being racist.

[MASK]’s guidance to the provider, which she acknowledged at the time was inaccurate, delayed the provider’s application and prevented him from receiving the proper credentials needed to practice within the Agency until the day his then-current privileges were set to expire.
